title: incident-preboarding-and-rapid-escalation-manual
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:
This page codifies a compact, reusable incident preboarding process and a rapid escalation manual for Redwood Inference on-call operators. It is intended to reduce time-to-stable for common serving and routing incidents by standardizing pre-incident checks, triage steps, escalation thresholds, customer notifications, and game-day exercises.

Who should use this doc:
- First responders and on-call SREs
- Bridge operators / duty leads
- Product engineers called for escalations
- Customer Success/Support for customer notices

Primary goals:
1) Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recover (MTTR) for latency and availability incidents.
2) Provide low-friction templates for the first 30 minutes of an incident (preboarding and initial comms).
3) Ensure consistent on-call handoffs and measurable follow-ups (postmortem + action tracking).

Scope and non-goals:
- Applies to Redwood hosted inference services (inference-gateway, routing-proxy, kv-cache, model-runtime).
- Not intended to replace service-specific deeper runbooks; those live under eng-serving-runtime/runbooks.
- This is not a legal or customer SLA explanation; use finance-and-legal templates for credits and contractual language.

Ownership and escalation contacts:
- Primary owner: SRE team (Pager: eng-sre-oncall)
- Escalation owner: Runtime Reliability (oncall: runtime-lead)
- Communications owner: Customer Success (oncall: cs-bridge)
- Exec escalation: Head of Production (oncall: prod-head)

Preboarding checklist (to run at sign-on or before a high-risk deploy):
- Confirm your PagerDuty roster and replacement on call.
- Confirm you have access: VPN, KMS keys, Debug bastion, Slack #incident, PagerDuty, Status Page admin.
- Load basic dashboards: "service-slo-overview", "token-latency-by-route", "error-rate-heatmap".
- Warm up common troubleshooting commands (see "Operator quick commands").
- Verify that postmortem template and a JIRA incident-ticket are ready (ticket prefix: INC-).

Incident lifecycle (concise numbered workflow):
1) Signal detection: automated SLO alert, customer report, or internal alert.
2) Acknowledge: on-call acknowledges in PagerDuty within 3 minutes for P0/P1.
3) Preboard (first 5 minutes): collect evidence, set bridge, record timeline.
4) Triage (5–15 minutes): classify impact, determine quick mitigations.
5) Mitigate (15–60 minutes): execute fixes or fallbacks, engage owners.
6) Stabilize (60+ minutes): confirm SLO recovery and route traffic back.
7) Communicate: send status page updates and customer templates per cadence.
8) Review: run postmortem within 72 hours and track action items to closure.

Priority definitions and SLO thresholds:
- P0 (SEV-0) — Platform outage: >30% of requests failing or latency >5x SLO for >5 minutes. Target MTTA: 1 minute, MTTR: 30 minutes.
- P1 (SEV-1) — Significant degradation: 5–30% of requests affected or sustained 2x latency for >5 minutes. Target MTTA: 3 minutes, MTTR: 2 hours.
- P2 (SEV-2) — Minor degradation or partial functional loss for a subset of tenants. MTTA: 30 minutes, MTTR: 24 hours.
- P3 (SEV-3) — Minor bug/feature regression with no immediate customer impact.

Rapid escalation matrix (use this table to decide whom to call and when):
| Time since detection | Trigger condition | Action | Escalation target | Notes |
|----------------------|-------------------|--------|-------------------|-------|
| 0–5m | P0 detection | Acknowledge & open bridge | On-call (primary) | DM runtime-lead in Slack #runtime-critical |
| 5–15m | No quick mitigation or impact grows | Page runtime-lead and product-owner | runtime-lead + product-owner | Consider traffic re-routing/fallback |
| 15–30m | SLO not recovering | Exec escalation (prod-head) + CS-bridge | prod-head, cs-bridge | Prepare customer comms and legal hold if needed |
| 30–60m | Ongoing customer-visible outage | Open cross-functional incident with engineering and support | All hands page | Trigger public status page updates and SOC brief |

Note: use PagerDuty for signal, Slack for rapid thread, and bridge (Zoom/Jitsi) for coordination. Place artifacts (logs, graphs) in the incident ticket.

Triage runbook: initial evidence and quick checks (first 10 minutes)
- Step 0: Capture scope: "Which services?" (inference-gateway, routing-proxy, kv-cache, model-runtime).
- Step 1: Validate SLO metric sources: Grafana dashboard (service-slo-overview), logs (elk/inference-logs), and tracing (jaeger).
- Step 2: Run automated checklist commands (examples):
  - Check gateway pods and recent restarts: kubectl -n production get pods -l app=inference-gateway -o wide
  - Check error ratios in last 5m: curl -s "http://monitoring/api/alerts?service=inference-gateway&window=5m" | jq .
  - Check KV cache eviction rates: curl -s http://kv-metrics/api | jq '.evictions_1m'
  - Confirm model runtime health: ssh runtime-bastion "systemctl status model-runtime || journalctl -u model-runtime -n 200"
- Step 3: Identify if a rollback or fallback can be applied quickly (traffic shift to previous model version, disable caching optimization).
- Step 4: If mitigation is not obvious, escalate per matrix and collect logs for postmortem.

Operator quick commands (cheat-sheet)
- Open bridge: ./scripts/open-bridge --incident INC-<id> --topic "inference outage"
- Post status update: ./scripts/statuspage post --component inference-gateway --status investigating --message "Investigating elevated errors"
- Rotate traffic to previous model (example): rd-ctl route set-weight --service inference-gateway --version v2025-09-20 --weight 100
- Flush KV cache for tenant (example): curl -X POST https://kv-cache.internal/flush?tenant=acme-corp --header 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

Status page templates (examples used by CS or Bridge operator)
- Initial: {
  "component": "inference-gateway",
  "status": "investigating",
  "message": "We are investigating elevated error rates impacting text generation. Impacted users may see failed requests or increased latency. We will update when we have more information."
}
- Update: {
  "component": "inference-gateway",
  "status": "degraded_performance",
  "message": "Mitigation in progress: traffic diverted to fallback model version v2025-09-20. Some requests may still fail intermittently. Next update in 30 minutes."
}
- Resolved: {
  "component": "inference-gateway",
  "status": "operational",
  "message": "Issue resolved. All services normal. Root cause investigation is ongoing and will be summarized in the postmortem."
}
(Replace values with real incident id and summary.)

Customer comms templates (concise, plain-language):
- Short initial email to affected customers:
  Subject: Redwood Inference – Service Interruption Update (INC-12345)
  Body: Hello <Customer>,
  We are aware of an issue affecting text generation for some requests. Our engineers are actively investigating. You may see errors or higher latency. We will provide our next update within 30 minutes. If you have critical workloads, please reply to this message and we will prioritize your tenant.
  — Redwood Inference Support

- Resolution notice to customers:
  Subject: Redwood Inference – Incident Resolved (INC-12345)
  Body: Hello <Customer>,
  The incident affecting text generation has been resolved at 2025-06-10T14:45Z. We restored traffic to the primary runtime and have confirmed system health. We are preparing a postmortem and will share findings and mitigations within 72 hours.

Postmortem and evidence collection (lightweight template):
- Title: INC-12345 — Elevated error rate impacting inference-gateway
- Timeline: (UTC timestamps, system detected, acknowledged, mitigation started, resolved)
- Impact: number of affected requests, percent of customers impacted, duration, SLO miss details
- Root cause: concise statement and supporting evidence (logs, diffs, commits)
- Contributing factors: list of 2–4 items (eg, config rollout, autoscaler threshold, false-positive alert)
- Corrective actions (owner, due date): eg, pin autoscaler version (owner: infra-team, due: 2025-07-01)
- Validation: how we will verify the fix (synthetic tests, canary metrics)
- Follow-ups: link to JIRA and next review meeting

Game-day & simulation plan (30–90 minute exercise template):
- Objective: validate that the on-call team can detect, escalate, and restore service within SLO targets using the preboarding steps.
- Participants: 1 bridge operator, 2 SREs (primary & secondary), 1 runtime engineer, 1 CS liaison.
- Scenario examples: high KV cache eviction causing 3x latency; model runtime OOM during peak; routing-proxy partial outage creating 50% of tenants with 500 errors.
- Schedule (example 60m):
  - 0–5m: Inject signal (monitoring alert + synthetic failing requests)
  - 5–15m: Triage & collect evidence. Bridge opens and status posted.
  - 15–30m: Apply mitigation (traffic shift, restart runtime, increase capacity).
  - 30–45m: Validate mitigation and prepare customer comm.
  - 45–60m: Debrief and write quick learning note; create postmortem ticket if relevant.
- Scoring rubric: detection time, acknowledgement time, mitigation time, customer comm quality. Capture metrics and iterate.

On-call rotation fairness & handoff checklist:
- Each shift should be no longer than 8 hours of primary on-call during weekdays and 12 hours on weekends (goal).
- Shadow rotations: new on-call shadow for first two shifts after onboarding.
- Handoff checklist (to be added to shift notes): last 3 incidents summary, outstanding action items, hotfixes applied, any experiments or deploys in progress.

Runbook governance and lifecycle:
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly by service owners.
- Deprecated runbooks are marked with label "runbook-deprecated" and archived after two quarters.
- Training: every engineer with on-call responsibilities must complete at least one game-day exercise per quarter.

Appendix: related templates and links
- Incident ticket template: jira/template/incident-basic
- Long-form runbooks: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/
- Monitoring dashboards: grafana/service-slo-overview
- Contact list: internal/contacts/oncall-directory

Quick references (cheat list):
- Urgent pager: @pagerduty eng-sre-oncall
- Bridge open script: ./scripts/open-bridge
- Status page CLI: ./scripts/statuspage

If you find gaps or have suggestions, add feedback to the page comments or open a small PR to this runbook.
